title: Until It Stands By Itself
logline: On open ground beside a village temple a heap of loose poles is stood up in groups whose tips cross and press on one another, held by hand and corrected for an hour, until at one moment every hand comes off at once and the frame carries itself — and then cloth, fronds and lamps are hung on it, which lean on it entirely and hold nothing up in return.
human_question: Between things standing next to each other and things holding each other up, what exactly is the difference?

place.what_kind_of_place: An open sandy yard beside a small village temple in the northern dry zone: red earth and grey sand, palmyra and coconut along the edges, a low wall, a gate, a tank or a creek not far off, and for most of the year nothing standing on the yard at all. In the week before the annual festival the yard becomes a site. The material arrives as raw stock and lies in heaps: long straight poles cut from areca, young coconut, kitul or bamboo, still with bark and taper, sorted roughly by length; coils of coir rope and cheap nylon twine; bundles of fresh fronds for the covering; and later, rolls of cloth, strings of small bulbs, cable, and a generator. The tools are a bush knife, a crowbar for starting holes, a ladder or two, and hands. The workforce is a mix: a few who have raised this frame every year for decades and know without measuring which pole goes where, and a larger number who are here because everybody is here. There is no drawing anywhere on the site.
place.why_it_is_worth_watching: Because the whole of it turns on one moment that either happens on camera or does not, and because the moment is physical and unmistakable. Up to it, nothing on the yard is stable: every pole is being held, propped, walked up, corrected, shouted about, and if one is let go the group it belongs to comes down. After it, nothing is being held at all, and a structure two or three times the height of a person stands on open sand carrying its own weight, with the tips of its poles crossing above and pressing on one another. Hands come off and people step back, and that is the event. From directly above, the crossing tips make a geometry that exists nowhere else and that you cannot see from the ground. And then the second half of the film is its own correction: everything the frame was built for — cloth, fronds, garlands, lamps, cable — goes onto it, hangs from it, depends on it completely, and contributes nothing whatever to it standing up. Both halves of the concept are physically present in the same object, in order, on the same afternoon.
place.what_moves_or_changes: Everything, within a week, and then back again. Bare yard, heaps of material, poles walked up, a frame, a covered frame, a lit frame, a crowd, and then a bare yard with the poles stacked and the sand raked. The frame itself is corrected constantly while it goes up: a pole is moved a hand's width, a lashing is redone, something settles overnight and is packed in the morning. Nothing about it is drawn or measured and nothing about it is permanent, and when it comes down the poles go back to whoever lent them and are used for something else. The only things that persist are the people who know how it is done and the yard.
place.when_it_looks_best: The festival week, which is fixed by its own calendar and not by the weather, so the film has no choice about the month. Within that week the raising is the one event that matters and it happens when the working party is ready, usually across a morning and an afternoon. Early and late light rakes across a forest of vertical poles on open sand and gives the best ground-level images; the overhead geometry of the crossing tips wants a high sun, because in low light the tips lose each other against the ground. The covered and lit frame belongs to dusk and to the dark. The empty yard before and after is worth filming in the same light as the frame, from the same positions, and is where the film starts and ends.

two_layers.without_the_philosophy: A film about a temporary structure going up by hand on open sand. Heaps of poles at first light; a crowbar starting a hole; a pole walked up hand over hand and held; three of them brought together at the tips and pressing; lashings, corrections, shouting, a pole moved a hand's width; the last one in and every hand coming off at once; people stepping back; the overhead geometry of crossed tips; then fronds, cloth, garlands, cable and lamps going on; the thing lit at dusk with a crowd under it not looking at it; and a week later, bare sand and a stack of poles. It has a complete shape with nothing said over it: nothing, a thing, nothing. Anyone who likes building, or the moment a structure takes its own weight, has a whole piece here.
two_layers.with_the_philosophy: The same afternoon becomes the source's own image for one named kind of support, and then becomes the source's own limit on it. The books define mutual support with sticks that stay upright only by leaning against one another at their tips, and in the very next sentence they say that not everything which arises together supports everything else, giving a case in which the support runs one way only. This film is that sentence and that next sentence, in that order, in one object: a frame that stands only by leaning, and decorations that hang on it and give it nothing. The voice is careful to say what it is not saying. This is one of twenty-four kinds of support and one of nine in the summary, most of which run in a single direction. It is not a picture of people helping each other, and it is not a warrant for saying that everything holds everything else up — which is exactly the claim the sources take trouble to refuse.

sequence.on_screen: First light on an open sandy yard beside a low temple wall. Nothing standing. Long poles in heaps sorted roughly by length, coils of rope, bundles of fresh fronds. A crowbar being worked into the sand to start a hole.
sequence.voice: This is raised in a week every year and taken down after. No drawing, no measurement, and nothing on this yard for the other fifty-one weeks. At the moment every single piece of it is lying on the ground.

sequence.on_screen: Three or four poles walked up hand over hand and brought together so that their tips cross and press. Hands on each one. Somebody lets go too early and the group starts to go over and is caught.
sequence.voice: The books have an image for one particular kind of support and it is this one. Several sticks, they say, stand upright without falling over by leaning against one another at their tips, and in that way they are a support to one another [C082-P:L3346]. That is the source's picture, not ours. It is also what is happening here.

sequence.on_screen: The lashing. Coir turned and hitched at a crossing. A pole moved a hand's width and the whole group settling. The last member in. Then every hand coming off at once, and people stepping back.
sequence.voice: Nothing was pulled here and nothing was dragged. It was stood up and made to lean. The same books say that nothing comes about from one thing alone, and their example is a match and the side of the box: two different helps, each working its own way, and if they worked the same way either one on its own would be enough [C082-M:L3].

sequence.on_screen: From directly above at high sun. The crossing tips, the pattern they make on the sand below, and the shadows of the poles. A geometry nobody standing under it can see.
sequence.voice: And then the limit, in the same passage, immediately after the sticks. Not everything that comes up together supports everything else. Some of what arises with a thing is held up by it and does not hold it up in return [C082-P:L3346]. The books repeat the same restriction elsewhere: what is derived is not a support for what is derived, and what the mind produces is no support for the mind [C082-P:L3616].

sequence.on_screen: The covering and the hanging. Fronds tied on, cloth unrolled over, garlands, a run of cable, strings of small bulbs. All of it going onto the frame and none of it going into the ground.
sequence.voice: Which is this half. Everything now going on depends on the frame completely and gives it nothing back. In the books' own terms, matter produced by the mind is only a thing conditioned and is never a condition for what produced it [C082-P:L2822]. Every part of what this was built for is in that position.

sequence.on_screen: A hand-copied list of the twenty-four names on a temple noticeboard or a schoolbook page, or simply the frame held still while the count is spoken. Then the frame again from the ground, complete.
sequence.voice: So the proportion matters. Leaning on each other is one item on a list of twenty-four kinds of support [C082-M:L9]. In the short summary it is one of nine ways that mind and matter together hold up mind and matter [C083-M:L29], and the summary's other five relations run in one direction only: mind to matter in one way, matter to mind in one way [C083-M:L5].

sequence.on_screen: Dusk and then dark. The frame lit, cloth moving, a crowd underneath, nobody looking at the structure. Then late, the crowd gone, the lamps still on, the poles visible again through the cloth.
sequence.voice: The summary does close wide, and it is worth having exactly right. There is no thing at all, past, present or future, inside a person or outside one, that is not a support for something; and everything except two is also held up by something [C083-M:L31]. That is a map with names on it. It is not the sentence that everything holds everything else up.

sequence.on_screen: A week later. Lashings cut, cloth off, poles walked down and stacked, holes filled, sand raked. The same first frame again: open yard, low wall, nothing standing.
sequence.voice: One more thing this is not. In the books, leaning is not people helping each other and not a village doing something together; it describes states inside a single moment of experience. What the film borrows is the picture and the restriction that comes with it, and the restriction is the half that usually gets left out.

concept_merge.why_together: C082 supplies both the image and its limit in a single passage, which is unusual and is the reason this film can be built at all. The section on mutuality defines it as the power by which mind and matter arising bound together in one moment support one another's arising and continuance, and illustrates it with several sticks that stand upright without falling only by leaning against each other at their tips; and the same passage goes straight on to say that not all the things which support by co-arising are also mutual conditions, giving as its case the matter produced by mind, which arises in the same instant and is supported by the mental states but is not a mutual condition for them [C082-P:L3346]. The same restriction is repeated in the section on ground: derived matter is not a ground for derived matter, and mind-produced matter is not a ground for the mind [C082-P:L3616]; and in the section on co-arising, mind-produced matter is listed as only a conditioned thing and never as a condition [C082-P:L2822]. Margaya supplies the frame around all of it: nothing arises from a single condition, argued with a match and the striking surface of the box, two helps of different kinds where one of the same kind twice would not do [C082-M:L3]; there is no phenomenon without some condition-power and some have many [C082-M:L7]; and the whole set is twenty-four [C082-M:L9]. C083 supplies the proportion the film has to state out loud. Its summary sorts all of it into six relations, of which mind supports mind in six ways, mind supports matter in one, matter supports mind in one, and mind and matter together support mind and matter in nine — and mutuality is one item inside that nine [C083-M:L5; C083-M:L29]. A frame that stands only by leaning, carrying decorations that hang on it and give it nothing, is the first concept's image and the first concept's limit standing on the same sand; and the second concept is what stops the image from being generalised.
concept_merge.what_it_reveals: That 'things hold each other up' is a claim that needs a direction attached to it before it means anything, and that the sources supply directions rather than a mood. Said flat, mutuality sounds like the group's title and like a warm idea about mutual dependence. Built on a yard it becomes a specific and rare thing with a visible boundary: this half of the object leans, that half only hangs, and the difference is not a matter of degree. The second concept keeps the film honest about scale by putting a number on it, one of twenty-four and one of nine, with most of the summary's relations running one way only. The slate already carries a film about a several-tonne chariot that moves only when many people pull at once, and this idea is deliberately built to be a different thing: nothing here is hauled, nothing is moved, nobody is pulling, and the event is a structure being made to stand rather than a mass being made to travel. The previous version of this idea centred the crew, their deadline, their pay and the risk of the structure failing on the day. That is dropped, because it made the concept a caption on a labour story and because it invited a collapse or a near-miss to become the film's drama.

concept_links.why: The digest's own image and the digest's own restriction are both narrated, in that order, over the footage each belongs to. The sticks leaning at their tips are spoken over poles being brought together and held, and are named out loud as the source's picture rather than the film's [C082-P:L3346]. The restriction that follows it in the same passage, that not everything arising together supports everything else and that some support runs one way only, is spoken over the overhead geometry, where the frame is complete and nothing has been hung on it yet [C082-P:L3346], and is reinforced with the parallel restrictions that derived matter is no ground for derived matter and that mind-produced matter is no ground for the mind [C082-P:L3616]. The one-way half is then shown rather than asserted, with the source's own instance spoken over the hanging: mind-produced matter is only conditioned and never a condition [C082-P:L2822]. Margaya's match and box carries the beat where the frame first stands, because that is where a single-cause account is most tempting [C082-M:L3], and the count of twenty-four is spoken plainly [C082-M:L9]. Every limit in the digest that bears on this film is honoured and two of them are beats. 'Everything is connected' is refused three times over and the group's own title is treated as the error. Mutuality is stated explicitly not to be social cooperation or community mutual aid, which is the digest's own correction and which matters here more than anywhere, because the footage is a crowd of villagers building something together and would otherwise say the opposite of the concept. The film makes no claim about ecology, networks or physics, and the match-and-box is spoken as the book's analogy rather than as doctrine. The six roots, predominance, proximity, kamma, repetition, nutriment, faculty, jhāna and path conditions are not narrated at all, so none of the digest's warnings about willpower, leadership, practice-makes-perfect, merit-as-possession or environment-as-destiny arise. The passages about the gravest acts and about fixed wrong view leading to hell are not cited, not narrated and not implied, and nothing about anybody on this yard is framed as an outcome of anything.

This concept exists in the film to state the proportion, and it is given two beats rather than a passing line because the digest's sharpest correction is exactly the one the footage invites. Mutuality is named as one item among the nine ways in which mind and matter together support mind and matter, and the surrounding relations are named as running one way: mind supports matter in one mode, matter supports mind in one mode [C083-M:L29; C083-M:L5]. Margaya's closing sweep is then given exactly as written, that there is no phenomenon of any time, inner or outer, that is not a support for something, and that everything but two is also supported — and the voice immediately says what that is and is not, because the digest's own reading is that support runs in specific nameable ways rather than as a vague sense that it is all connected [C083-M:L31]. Every limit in the digest is honoured. 'Everything is mutually interdependent' is the digest's named distortion and is refused in as many words in the sixth beat, which is the reason this concept is linked at all. 'Mind over matter' and 'matter over mind' are avoided by quoting the traffic in both directions as one mode each rather than glossing either. The claim about later mind supporting earlier body is not narrated, so no health or willpower reading can arise. The point that concepts are real conditions for the mind is not used, because this film has no footage for it and the digest's caution about it is better served by silence.

what_the_viewer_could_understand: That in this analysis some things stand only because they hold each other up in the same instant, that this is a specific named kind of support with the source's own picture attached to it, that it is one of twenty-four and one of nine and that most of the relations on the list run in a single direction, and that a great deal of what stands together is only being carried and gives nothing back. The frame is an analogy for one named relation and the film says so; nothing here describes how people should treat each other, and nobody on the yard is an example of anything.
what_must_be_real: The raising as the working party does it, on its own day and in its own order. Nothing is staged, re-raised, dismantled for a second angle, slowed, or held so that a shot can be made, and the moment the frame first carries itself is either filmed as it happens or is not in the film. No collapse, near-miss or failure is arranged, encouraged or dramatised, and if something does come down it is filmed only if nobody is hurt and the people involved are content for it to be used. Nobody is asked to hold a pole for the camera. The film does not put any individual forward as the one who knows how it is done, and it does not interview anybody about the structure. The temple and the working party decide where the camera may stand and when it must not be in the air, and the film does not intrude on the ritual the frame is built for: the festival is filmed as the reason the object exists, not as the film's subject, and no act of worship is used as an illustration of anything.
position_hint: late in the group, after the films that follow a chain forward and carry continuity across time, because it introduces a kind of support that is not sequential at all and because it is the group's explicit correction of its own title. It should sit before any film that relies on the twenty-four-fold list having been named once, and it must not sit next to the slate's film about a chariot moved by simultaneous effort. No location reasoning is involved.
risks: The single largest risk: a crowd of villagers building something together reads as community cooperation, which is precisely what the source says mutuality is not, so the film would show the opposite of its own concept unless the correction is stated plainly and early.
Generalising the image into the group's title, so that one of twenty-four relations becomes a claim that everything holds everything else up.
Dropping the one-way half, which is the harder half and the half that is always cut, leaving a warm film about leaning.
Reading like the slate's chariot film: any language of pulling, hauling, dragging or moving together belongs to that film and not to this one, which is about standing, not travelling.

Making the build into a race against a deadline, with pay, reputation and the possibility of failure as the stakes, which is what the earlier version of this idea did and which turns the concept into a caption.
Waiting for or encouraging a collapse, or using a genuine near-miss as the film's peak.
Filming a religious festival as spectacle, or letting acts of worship become illustrations of Abhidhamma.
Filming in a district with a heavy recent war history in a way that either exploits that history or pretends it is not there; neither is this film's subject and both are present in the ground.
Putting the camera or a drone where a pole can come down on somebody, or where it distracts the people holding one.
drop_if: No frame of this kind is raised inside the filming window, or the structure now arrives ready-made in sections so that nothing is stood up on site.
The working party will not have a camera present during the raising, which is the one event the film is built on.
The structure is raised with scaffold clamps, bolted steel or guy lines rather than by leaning and lashing, so the source's image is not on screen.
Filming positions that are safe during the raising cannot be found, or the only way to film the key moment is to ask for it to be repeated.
Permission for the festival ground cannot be had on terms that keep worship out of the film's argument.

connections.note: A covering that holds across years by being wholly replaced is followed by a frame that holds in one instant because its parts press on each other, and the second film has to say that the two are different kinds of support.
Both films turn on a restriction the source insists on rather than on the idea it is famous for, and both have to state what their own footage would otherwise be taken to mean.

selection.reason: The source's own image for mutuality and the source's own limit on it are physically present in one object, in order, on one afternoon, and the moment every hand comes off at once is both the best shot and the concept.

review.note: Rewritten 2026-09-24 into the footage-led shape. What was dropped: the crew as subject, the deadline, the pay and reputation, and the possibility of the structure failing on the day. Those made the film a labour story with the concept as its caption, and they put a collapse in the position of the film's climax, which is not something a film may want to happen. What is kept and sharpened: the leaning image and, more importantly, the restriction that follows it in the same passage of the source, which now has a beat of its own and is not allowed to be a footnote. The film is deliberately built to be a different object from the slate's existing film about a several-tonne chariot that moves only on simultaneous effort: nothing here is hauled or moved, nobody pulls, and the event is a structure made to stand rather than a mass made to travel; the risks list makes that separation explicit. The supporting concept was given two beats rather than one because its digest names 'everything is mutually interdependent' as the distortion to refuse, and because the footage is a crowd building something together and would otherwise say exactly that. Both digests were re-read from scratch and every citation was verified line by line against the source files; the old idea carried no citations at all.

suggested_location.name: The festival pandal ground of a village kovil at Mulliyawalai, Mullaitivu District

also_known_as.name: pandal / pandhal
also_known_as.meaning: the temporary pole-and-frond pavilion raised for a temple festival, from which cloth, garlands and lamps are hung
also_known_as.used_by: Tamil and general south Asian usage

also_known_as.name: Mulliyavalai
also_known_as.meaning: an alternative spelling of the same town, which is divided into five village officer divisions

also_known_as.name: kaddu kovil
also_known_as.meaning: a small jungle-side temple, as distinct from the larger institutions on the main roads

suggested_location.region: Mullaitivu District, Northern Province: the inland town and its surrounding village officer divisions, a few kilometres from the coast on the road south from the district town, in palmyra, paddy and scrub country
suggested_location.why_here: Because the district is among the thinnest on this slate, because small village temples here still raise their festival frames from raw poles on open sand rather than hiring sectional staging, and because the ground itself suits the one shot the film needs: flat red and grey sand, low walls, scattered palmyra, and yards that are empty for most of the year, so a structure can be isolated from directly overhead with nothing else in the frame. The town is a real place of about four and a half thousand people divided into five village officer divisions, with more than one small temple rather than a single dominant institution, which means the film can look for a modest yard and a modest working party instead of a major festival. A small temple is also the right scale for the concept: a frame two or three times the height of a person, raised in an afternoon by a few dozen people who all know each other, where a single pole can be seen to matter and the moment every hand comes off is legible in one shot. And the covering and hanging that follow are unambiguous: fronds, cloth, garlands and lamps, all of them carried entirely by the frame and contributing nothing to it.
what_to_film: The yard empty, from a fixed position, in the same light as the finished frame will be filmed in, at the start and at the end.
The material as stock: heaps of poles sorted by length with bark and taper still on them, coils of coir, bundles of fresh fronds, and a crowbar starting a hole in sand.
One group of poles walked up and brought together so the tips cross and press, held by hand, with somebody letting go too early and the group being caught.
The lashing at arm's length: coir turned and hitched at a crossing, and a pole moved a hand's width with the whole group settling.
The moment every hand comes off at once and people step back, in one shot from a position chosen in advance. This is the film and it happens once.
The crossing tips from directly above at high sun, with the pattern of the poles' shadows on the sand below.
The covering and the hanging: fronds tied on, cloth unrolled, garlands, cable and strings of bulbs, all of it going onto the frame and none of it into the ground.
The frame lit at dusk with people underneath and nobody looking at it.
The dismantling a week later: lashings cut, poles walked down and stacked, holes filled, sand raked.
A pole that is visibly older and more used than the rest, held still, without commentary.
suggested_location.access: By road from the district town. Everything depends on the temple and its working party agreeing well in advance, and on the film being attached to a festival that is happening anyway, on its own calendar. This district carries a very heavy recent war history, with commemoration, land release and military presence all live issues, and religious gatherings here have been reported as taking place under surveillance; a crew has to understand that context before arriving, must not become part of it, and must be prepared to be refused or to be watched. Drone flight in this part of the north is not something to assume and would need clearance as well as the temple's agreement, and it must not be in the air while poles are being stood up. Filming positions during the raising are decided by the working party, not by the camera.
suggested_location.best_time: The festival week, which is fixed by the temple's own calendar and not by weather or by the film. Within it, the raising day, which is decided by the working party and cannot be moved; a high sun for the overhead geometry of the crossing tips; early and late light for the forest of poles on open sand; dusk and full dark for the lit and covered frame; and a separate return for the dismantling, which is a week later and is the film's last shot.

suggested_location.research_note: Desk research only, and unverified on the ground. From the sources above: the town named in the coordinates is in this district, is divided into five village officer divisions and had a population of about 4,647 at the 2012 census; a pandal is a temporary or permanent fabricated structure raised outside a building or in an open area, commonly built of wood and cloth over a bamboo superstructure, and is used in this country at both Hindu and Buddhist festivals; the district's best-known coastal shrine holds a large annual festival some kilometres north of the town, and press reporting describes religious gatherings in this district taking place under military surveillance. The coordinates are the published position of the town and are a direction towards its temple yards, not a survey: no temple, yard, working party or festival date has been identified or approached, and the film is deliberately proposed for a small village temple rather than the district's major shrine. The film's central assumption is an inference and not a confirmed fact about this town: that a festival frame here is still raised from raw poles stood up and lashed on site, by leaning rather than by bolted or clamped staging, and that the moment it first carries itself is a real and observable event. That should be checked with the temple before anything else, and if the frames here arrive in sections the idea has to move rather than be staged. No permission has been sought from any temple, working party or authority, and no photograph of a pandal being raised, or of any festival frame in this district, was found on Wikimedia Commons; the two images are of a small temple in the named town and of a waterway in the district.

unknowns: Whether festival frames here are still stood up from raw poles and lashed on site, or arrive as sectional staging, which is the question that decides whether the film exists.
Whether the structure is genuinely held by leaning and lashing rather than by guy lines, clamps or bolts, since the source's image depends on it.
When the raising happens inside the festival week, and whether the moment the frame first carries itself is a single identifiable event or is spread over hours.
Whether a temple and its working party will have a camera present during the raising, and where it would be allowed to stand.
Whether any aerial view can be obtained in this district at all, and whether the overhead geometry of the crossing tips can be filmed safely.
Whether the film can be made here without becoming entangled in the district's commemoration politics or in the surveillance of religious gatherings reported there.
evidence_class_note: Editorial proposal. The location is proposed by Claude from desk research and is unverified. No scene or shot is decided here.
